trigger_phrase: I don't want another bill.
response_agree: Completely understand, sir. A lot of homeowners say the same thing—they don't want another stressor.
response_resume: That's why this isn't about adding a bill. We're aiming to eliminate your electric bill completely and replace it with one that's usually 30 to 50% cheaper.
framework_step: Agree -> Answer -> Bridge -> Note -> Fair? -> Resume

trigger_phrase: My electricity bills are already low.
response_agree: Got it. If you don't mind me asking—how much are you currently paying?
response_resume: If >$150: Perfect. We can probably reduce that significantly. If <$60: I'll be honest, sir, it might not be worth it for you, and we'd likely disqualify the property. If $60-150: In that range, we can usually still help you save and lock in a fixed rate—so you're not at the mercy of rate hikes every month. Wouldn't it be nice to just know exactly what you're paying, no surprises?

trigger_phrase: What's the catch?
response_agree: Sir, the only catch is—you need to qualify.
response_resume: That's what this whole call is about. If you qualify, you simply switch to a better energy provider at a locked-in, lower rate.

trigger_phrase: I don't want to finance anything.
response_agree: Absolutely, sir. And just to clarify—we're not getting you into any traditional loans.
response_resume: You're simply switching from one electric provider (that charges more) to another that charges less. Your payment just becomes more stable and more affordable. That's it.

trigger_phrase: I want to wait until prices drop.
response_agree: I totally get that instinct, sir.
response_resume: The thing is—with inflation, nothing is actually getting cheaper. Even as tech improves, prices usually go up, not down. So waiting won't mean a better deal—it often means you miss the window to lock in lower rates now.

trigger_phrase: My credit isn't good.
response_agree: Thanks for being honest, sir. We actually have a few options here.
response_resume: Is there anyone else on the home who has a credit score above 650? If yes: we can likely use their credit to get you qualified. If no: is there anyone close to you who would be willing to co-sign or be included to help you qualify? If unsure: do you know your approximate credit score? I can check with my manager if it's something we can still work with.

trigger_phrase: I rent / I'm not the homeowner.
response_agree: Got it—thank you for letting me know.
response_resume: Unfortunately, this program is only available to homeowners. If you have a landlord or know who owns the property, I'd be happy to speak with them to see if they'd be interested. They could benefit from solar while the tenant still pays the bill, which means they get the tax credit and increase the property value.
framework_step: Disqualify path with landlord referral offer

trigger_phrase: I have a tenant living there.
response_agree: That's totally fine, sir.
response_resume: We've helped many landlords install solar on rental properties. The best part is: your tenant continues to pay for power, but you get the financial benefit—like the tax credit and added property value. We'd just need to make sure it's set up correctly with ownership.

trigger_phrase: I'm planning to move.
response_agree: Thanks for sharing that, sir. Just so I'm clear—when exactly are you planning to move?
response_resume: If <6 months: Understood, it might make sense to wait until you're in your new home. If >6 months: Great, that still gives you time to benefit, and when you sell, the new owner benefits too—have you listed the home yet? If not listed: then the move is still in the planning phase, and this could reduce costs while you're still there.

trigger_phrase: I'm planning to do home renovations (kitchen, roof, etc.).
response_agree: Sir, I'm actually glad I caught you right now.
response_resume: We might be able to get that kitchen you're planning to renovate completely for free. The government is currently incentivizing solar projects, and they allow home renovation work to be bundled into the solar financing—potentially covering 30% of it through the federal tax credit. In some cases, we can even take a portion of our commission to help cover the cost upfront. So this might be the perfect timing.

trigger_phrase: My cousin/friend had a bad experience with solar.
response_agree: Totally understand, sir. I honestly don't know what happened with other companies—but I can tell you we're not here scamming people.
response_resume: We're just booking appointments with homeowners in your area to see if solar would help them save. That's it. If they insist: ask what happened and let them speak, then offer to send the engineer out with the cousin present too, to walk through everything and avoid the same issues.

trigger_phrase: Can you just send me an email?
response_agree: Yes, absolutely—what's your email, sir?
response_resume: Perfect. So in order to send you the right information, I do need to ask you a couple of quick questions first—just to make sure your home actually qualifies. Then we can pass that along to the engineer so they can build a personalized report. Normally the engineer does need to swing by to check your meter and some basic info. If everything checks out, they can show you the report right there, and if you still want it by email, we can send it after that.
framework_step: Capture email -> Redirect to qualifying questions -> Bridge to appointment
